findings: Novelty remains materially unresolved: artifacts/contract.json and artifacts/selected.json acknowledge that historical PR684 tests the same essential selective-aperture sifting ability. The contract therefore correctly blocks development pending a fresh catalog, team-history, and ownership review; the available six-suite comparison does not resolve that historical task-level overlap.

The pre_batch_aperture_credit_latch_control is internally inconsistent. Under scoring_spec, when F first reaches 1 and every washer is in the screen, batch_established latches immediately; previously crossed media currently in the receiver then becomes recovery-eligible, making the score greater than 0.20. The stated 0.20 outcome is only possible if r=0, which does not test deferred pre-batch aperture credit. The control must specify crossed-media mass and the exact observation/event ordering, then recompute the expected score.

The other required-control scores recompute consistently: initial 0; loaded 0.20; r=0.49 gives 0.55; r>=0.98 without dwell gives 0.90; 720 intervals gives 1.00; 719 gives 0.90; hard failures give 0; apparatus caps give 0.10/0.20; washer caps give 0.20/0.40; simultaneous caps give 0.20; complete media spill leaves 0.20; dwell revocation leaves 0.90. Timeout processing and timing are consistent: 4,800 actions at 20 Hz equals 240 s, with 57,600 intervals at 240 Hz and 115,200 refinement intervals at 480 Hz.

Several robot-level physics checks remain underspecified despite the repaired component procedures: bilateral_screen_grip_contact_duration_min does not define qualifying collider pairs or continuity/reset aggregation; loaded_screen_lift_height_min lacks its reference height and sampled screen point; loaded_screen_lift_hold_duration_min does not define whether the hold must be continuous or which predicate resets it; joint-limit margins do not identify the evaluated trajectory or aggregation interval. These observables are not yet independently computable.

No input/runtime-api-preflight.json or input/pinned-runtime-sources snapshot is present. The contract appropriately treats 20 Hz control, 240/480 Hz physics, and the guarded 14D interface as prospective, but runtime compatibility cannot be verified at this gate.
